label: In development
blurb: Merged, not yet in a numbered release.

groups.name: New
items: Export to PNG. Lossless and 16-bit, with the same frame, watermark and metadata as every other format.
A RAW opens at the aspect ratio set in the camera. Shot at 16:9 or 1:1, it opens cropped to that, with the rest of the sensor one drag or one Free away.
Drag the histogram to move a tone slider. Blacks, Shadows, Exposure, Whites and Highlights each have a zone on the graph; hover to see which, then drag.
Build a brush mask up gradually. Flow sets how much each stroke adds and Strength how far it can go; [ and ] resize the brush.
Paint a mask that stays on one colour. Turn on Match Color for the brush and a stroke only takes on colours like the one where it starts — the sky, not the branches in front of it.
Mask one person, not everyone. A People mask lists who is in the photo, by name when the People tab knows them, and One Mask per Person gives each their own.
Hide the Develop sections you don't use. Right-click a section header on Edit or Grading and choose Show/Hide Sections…; a hidden section keeps its edits.

See where the camera focused. Show focus point (⇧E) marks it on Canon, Fujifilm, Nikon, Olympus / OM System, Panasonic and Sony photos, in the Lightbox, Compare, Survey, Develop and the grid's magnifier.
Shape the Color Mixer as a curve. Add your own points between its eight colours, for a sky between Aqua and Blue or skin between Red and Orange.
Choose what a preset carries, slider by slider, and sort presets into categories. A new preset leaves exposure and white balance alone unless you tick them.
Darken or lighten the corners with a vignette. It follows your crop, and Midpoint, Roundness, Feather and Highlights shape it.

See an HDR merge before it is written, and choose how it is made. HDR Merge Preview lets you pick the frame it is anchored on, how strongly moving things are kept out and whether to align and crop, with an overlay showing where it decided.

groups.name: Changed
items: Click an object to mask it on a cropped, straightened or lens-corrected photo too.
At startup Chili RAW re-reads only the folders that changed since it last ran.
Deleting a photo inside Chili RAW marks its folder with the amber dot until you synchronize the folder or undo the delete.
Focus peaking works in the Lightbox, Compare, Survey and Develop, not only the grid's Loupe: one switch, and E toggles it anywhere.
Copy Settings lists every slider, and Crop can copy just the aspect ratio, centred on each photo.
Decimals follow your Mac's region. Where your region writes numbers with a comma, readouts show 1,5 EV rather than 1.5 EV.

groups.name: Fixed
items: The amber dot marks folders changed while Chili RAW was closed, and synchronizing one folder leaves every other folder's dot in place.
A missing photo shows Media Offline in the filmstrip.
Lift & Stamp copies Color Mixer, Color Grading and Grain.
HDR merges keep the full resolution of the original photos. Brackets from some cameras used to come out at a reduced size.
JPEG brackets merge properly. Every frame now counts, where the merge used to keep mostly one of them, and blown areas fill in without flat grey patches.
A bracket shot RAW+JPEG merges its raw files. The JPEGs are left out instead of being mixed in with them.
Handheld HDR brackets line up. Frames shot without a tripod used to be shifted further apart instead of together, and much of the picture was left out as if it had moved.

groups.name: New
items: Export every version of a photo, not just the live one. Tick Include all versions and each one writes its own file, named after the version it came from.
Put back an earlier copy of a folder's edits. File ▸ Earlier Copies of This Folder… lists what Chili RAW has kept for it, so a change you regret can be walked back one folder at a time.
A backup drive that would silently lose your edits is caught before you rely on it. Some drives and sync folders quietly discard them when you mirror your photos, and the Backups settings now say so.
Restore from a backup. Pick one, confirm, and your edits, presets, albums, Looks, LUTs, watermarks, named faces and photo folders come back — your photo files are never touched.
Look inside a backup before you need it. File ▸ Look Inside a Backup… shows what a backup holds — your edits, named faces, presets and albums — and flags any photo folder that is not on this Mac.
The full right-click menu, everywhere a photo is — the filmstrip in Develop, Pixels, Compare and the Lightbox, and the Lightbox photo itself.
Arrange the Develop panel your way. Drag a section by its header, or right-click it to move it. Edit and Grading each keep their own order.
A watermark on export. Text or a PNG on every copy a batch writes, in one of nine positions, previewed before it runs.
A border round your photos on export — any thickness, in white, black or grey. Pro adds 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16 shapes.
Frames in Pixels, in the photo's own colours. A Mount grows the canvas around the picture rather than painting over it, and survives an export.
Switch a RAW+JPEG pair with one click. A corner badge says which file you are looking at; click it for the other one. Each keeps its own edits.
Chili RAW is in the Shortcuts app — export with a preset, apply a develop preset, set a rating, set a flag. Pro.

groups.name: Changed
items: The Neutral tone mode is now called Minimal, and it now lives up to it. It adds no look of its own, so a film Look or a LUT starts from a clean image — at the cost of highlights that clip rather than roll off.
The People mask is now called Person. The People view, where you name faces, is unchanged.
Generative Remove no longer appears when a Person mask is narrowed to a face part. Erasing someone's lips or eyes was never a useful edit; it stays for Whole person.
The mask panel no longer explains Generative Remove at length. The button is where it was, with the sliders back in easy reach under it.
Film Labor's Grain slider reaches much further. What used to be full strength sits about a third of the way along it now, so grain shows where it was barely there before.
The Film Labor picture is sharper on a large window, and grain there now reads the way it does in an exported file.
Zooming into the Film Labor picture shows real detail. Past Fit you now see the grain your file will have, rather than a magnified version of the small one.
A film stock now arrives at 75 % strength rather than full, on a Look slider that is longer than it was, so small adjustments are easier to make.
The Film Stock swatches are gone from the Grading panel. LUTs are now the one place for a film look — import a .cube of your own, or link a folder of them.

groups.name: Fixed
items: A Person mask's Hair no longer stops in a straight line across the photo. Long hair is now masked to its ends, and Neck and Clothing reach as far as they need to.
Thumbnails keep filling in while you edit. In a folder of edited photos the filmstrip and the grid used to stop on grey placeholders for seconds at a time.
Turning on lens corrections no longer closes the app. Ticking Enable Profile Corrections in Develop ▸ Geometry now reads the photo's built-in correction data without interrupting the panel.

The filter band lays out properly in a narrow window. The count and its two buttons drop below the filters instead of squeezing them into a corner, the columns spread to fill each line, and the number of photos shown no longer breaks across two lines.
Develop tabs remember where you were. Geometry opens at the top the first time instead of part way down, and after that each tab comes back to the spot you left it.
A backup that fails now says so, and names what it couldn't copy — with a Copy Details button in Settings ▸ Backups for the full list.
A failed backup no longer replaces the one you already had. Backing up twice in one day, with the second attempt failing, used to leave you with neither.
Renaming the backup subfolder no longer doubles your library, or empties it when a folder above your photos happens to share the name.
The hidden safety copies no longer pile up. Each is removed once the write it protects is confirmed good, instead of staying on your drive for ever.
The safety-copy folder can no longer be renamed. A name you already chose keeps working.
Two photo folders with the same name both make it into a backup. Only the first used to; the second's edits were left out without a word.
Old backups are cleared away. The ten most recent dated backups are kept and older ones removed, instead of one building up per day for ever.
A backup now carries every face you have named. Detection can find the faces again, but never who they are.
A backup now carries your export presets, your watermarks and your photo folders, so a restore gives back the export side of the app too.
The restore notes inside a backup now cover everything in it — the catalog and your edits, not only the app's own settings — and say how to put each piece back.
A film look no longer flattens the brightest parts of a photo. The sun, a lamp or a bright reflection kept its shape instead of turning into a flat patch of sky.
Print Character now relaxes the paper instead of darkening the picture. Turning it down used to deepen the shadows; it opens them.
Renaming several photos at once no longer empties the folder.
A renamed photo keeps everything you gave it — its people, its film look, its collections and its RAW+JPEG side choice.
A launch can no longer stall on a blank screen.
A chosen crop ratio now holds while you drag.
A cropped photo fills the Develop canvas again.
A backup now carries your imported LUTs, your starred LUTs and your saved Looks, along with the folder you linked them from.
The histogram follows a clip while it plays instead of freezing on the frame you started from.
Darkroom (⌃⌘F) now clears the whole screen, Develop panel and filmstrip included, and takes the window full-screen. ⌃⌘F again brings it all back.
Switching folders with a filter on no longer closes the app. Filtering the grid and then clicking another folder in the sidebar could quit Chili RAW.

groups.name: New
items: Chili RAW updates itself — Settings ▸ Updates offers a new version and puts it in place, with no disk image to drag.
Every mask row shows what it selects: a small map of the frame with that mask's own coverage lit up.
⌘Z undoes a develop edit, ⇧⌘Z puts it forward, and each photo keeps its own history.
Choose what the photo is judged against — Settings ▸ General ▸ Photo surround: black, white or a custom grey.
Drag a layer row anywhere to reorder the stack, thumbnail included.
Duplicate a mask, or duplicate it inverted, from the right-click menu.
Masks have names — numbered as you make them, and renameable.
Bloom, a diffusion glow at the head of the Film Labor chain. Off by default.
Point at the photo, see where it lands on the scope, with the pixel's R/G/B read out.
Faces get their own cluster in the vectorscope, against the skin-tone line.
Five scopes in Develop, where the histogram used to be: RGB Overlay, RGB Split, Waveform, RGB Parade and Vectorscope.
A ghost of the unedited photo, under the live trace.
The clipping percentages are buttons — click one and those pixels are painted on the photo.
Two export favourites, on ⌘E and ⇧⌘E, both rebindable.
Export straight from the Lightbox, with your saved presets in its top bar.
Fold the filmstrip away with ⌥T, across the Lightbox, Compare, Develop and Pixels.
Choose where AI models are stored — Settings ▸ AI ▸ Model location. Models you already have are moved, not downloaded again.

groups.name: Changed
items: Pixels sits the photo on the same surround as everywhere else.
The tone curve tells you which way is which — channel colours, a percentage on every point, and Blacks · Midtones · Whites along the foot.
The film and paper lists only show stocks you can actually use: 29 film profiles across 17 stocks, 4 slide films and 8 papers.
LibRaw is no longer marked experimental.
Film grain on screen now matches the grain in the exported file. Exported files are unchanged, to the byte.
Chili RAW brings its own Perl, so a macOS update cannot take your metadata tools away.
Dark edges inside blown highlights no longer flash black.
Less magenta fizz along blown highlights, on DxO and other linear DNGs.
The shadow-clipping overlay works again, on any window size.
The clipping percentages count your photo's pixels, not a blurred copy — expect both figures to read higher.
The Develop preview goes straight from the graphics card to the screen.
Resizing the window no longer re-develops the photo while you drag.
The filmstrip no longer measures the whole folder on every frame.
The Settings window is taller, so the longer tabs no longer open already scrolled.
The Export dialog stops growing instead of stretching across a big display.
The Lightbox is one photo at a time, and hands your grid selection back when you leave.
⌘C shows the Copy Settings dialog once, then copies silently. ⌘⇧C brings it back.
The floating Lift & Stamp panel is gone; the dialog replaced it.

groups.name: Fixed
items: Film Labor's small text is readable again, on both themes.
Small text across the app is readable now, on both themes — worst on Neutral Grey.
Lens profile corrections no longer leave a black border.
Masks and repairs stay on what you put them on when Lens Corrections is switched on.
Film Labor's controls show you when they can't do anything, with one line saying what is missing.
Leaving the Lightbox puts you back where you were.
The AI keyword buttons say what they are doing, with a progress bar and a Stop.
Keyword suggestions no longer stay dead until you relaunch.
Renaming a photo keeps everything that belonged to it — ratings, flags, labels, edits, versions, masks, faces and stack membership.
Switching folders no longer writes a blank sidecar over the folder you left.
A RAW and its JPEG stop wiping each other's keywords.
Exporting a clip over an existing file no longer deletes that file when the export then fails.
Deselecting actually deselects, so the next ⌫, Export or cull acts on what you can see.
"Edits only" backups keep every saved version, not just the active one.
Saving edits no longer destroys masks written by a newer build.
Clicking in and out of a mixed field leaves it mixed.
Colour label "None" sticks.
Capture times are read in the photo's own offset, not shifted by yours.
Synchronize Folder picks up sidecar edits made in another app.
Two exports running at once no longer clobber each other.
Healing at the very edge of the frame no longer crashes.
A corrupt lens-correction block in a DNG no longer hangs the render.
The grain swatch and the clip player no longer read memory that has already gone.
Cancelled background work stops overwriting the work that replaced it.
Auto Sync stops replacing crops you placed by hand.
Selecting a saved Wand mask just selects it.
Film Labor no longer saves a Look you never chose, and its stock rows follow the develop settings.
Printer lights are visible and editable on Scan output.
Blacks no longer flattens saturated out-of-gamut colour.
A mask's Dehaze works on a cropped or straightened photo.
Heal stops sampling the blemish it is removing on portrait frames.
APS-C bodies that aren't in the lens database are no longer over-corrected.
Semi-transparent gradients render at their real colour, and text exports in the font it previewed in.
Small images are no longer crushed to 8-bit before an upscale.
Before/after shows the before frame at the right shape, not stretched.
The half-brite toggle in Pixels is reversible, ramp edits stop permuting the picture, and empty layers survive into a PSD or TIFF.
Depth-based masks stop serving a stale coverage figure.
Installed AI models are reported as installed.
Leaving Compare or Survey keeps your grid selection.
Version compare commits the version you can see.
Tiles re-sharpen when you change the tile size.
The folder tint and the AI mark can't end up the same colour.
⌘Z undoes typing in the filter field, a rename, or a preset name.
Rebinding Proof to x no longer kills Reject permanently.
The Brush Size slider has its full travel.
Removing a location clears both Latitude and Longitude.
The export name preview matches the files you get.
Places at the very edge of the search radius are found, and accented names match everywhere.
The map keeps up on large folders, and follows a theme change without a relaunch.
Face crops are cleaned up when their photos go, and merging two groups keeps the cover you picked.
4-colour DNGs decode with the fourth channel at the right brightness.
⌘Z undoes your typing in a filter box, a rename or a preset name.
The white balance reading belongs to the photo you are looking at, showing … until it arrives.
Brush strokes step aside while you move a slider — hold O to see them.
The count on a map cluster is readable on the grey theme.
Typing a place no longer pushes the map's Standard / Places buttons down the screen.

groups.name: New
items: Lens Corrections (Develop ▸ Geometry) — distortion, vignetting and fringing, off by default. Reads your camera's own correction tables where the file carries them (Sony ARW, Fujifilm RAF, DNG), a bundled Lensfun database otherwise, plus manual sliders for lenses nothing has measured.
Edit many photos at once. Auto Sync applies the control you move to the whole selection, live — Edit and Grading tabs, plus aspect ratio, rotation and flips.
Auto Level a whole selection, each photo measured on its own. Photos with no level reference are left alone and counted.
Enlarge in Pixels (E) — click an object and scale it up to 400 % in place. Exports at full resolution and travels into a layered PSD/TIFF.
Generative Remove from a selection you already have — an Object, Subject, Sky, People or Depth mask, instead of painting.
Six more Film Labor papers: Supra Endura, Endura Premier, Crystal Archive DPII, Fujiflex, 2393 Vision Premier, Eterna-CP 3513DI. Eight in all.
The sidebar folds away to a thin rail — ⌥\, or the ‹ in its top-right corner. Rebindable.
Zoom in Pixels — ↑/↓, Z to fit, Space-drag to pan.
AI model updates — Settings ▸ AI flags a model with a newer version and offers Update. Nothing downloads by itself.
A photo carrying a film Look is marked — an amber filmstrip on the grid tile, a Film pill on the Develop canvas.

groups.name: Changed
items: Highlights recovery now works on Sony, Canon, Nikon and Fujifilm raws, not only on DNG.
Blown highlights rebuild neutral instead of drifting peachy.
Generative Remove reconstructs large areas at 1024 px instead of 512. Delete and re-download the model in Settings ▸ AI to get it.
Print Exposure reads as brightness — up is lighter. Saved Looks render exactly as before.
Develop keeps your selection — arrow keys move through it, ⌘-click and ⇧-click build it in the filmstrip.
Grain on formats larger than 35 mm now gets finer on screen too, not only in an export.

groups.name: Fixed
items: Switching version switches its Film Labor Look with it, and Compare Versions renders each pane with its own version's film.
Changing the RAW decoder, or the LibRaw colour profile, re-renders edited raw thumbnails. (An unedited raw shows the camera's own preview and is unaffected.)
A blend layer is developed with the decoder you have selected.
Re-importing a .cube, or editing one in a linked folder, updates the thumbnails.
Heal, Clone and Detect Spots work on a cropped or straightened photo.
Visualize Spots is framed like the photo rather than the whole sensor frame.
Composition guides stay on when you change photo.
Auto Sync matches white balance by Kelvin, so a batch lands on the same temperature. JPEGs in a raw selection are skipped and reported.
A manual lens slider no longer drops the file's own built-in correction.
"Landscape" fits on one line in Crop ▸ Aspect ratio.
The Lift & Stamp close button is a normal-sized target.

groups.name: New
items: Generative Remove — paint over something and the background is rebuilt around it, on your Mac, on a model you download. No text prompt: it makes things disappear rather than adding new ones. Regions are listed and can be extended, switched off or deleted.
Search your photos by what's in them — type "red car at sunset", or right-click a photo for Find Similar. Indexing runs in the background, and the app can suggest keywords.
AI Denoise — high-ISO noise removal that works on every RAW path, with a strength slider.
AI upscaling on export — SPAN, Real-ESRGAN or the macOS 4× scaler, chosen by how far you are enlarging and how big the source is, with a side-by-side compare in the export sheet.
AI tools are colour-marked — teal for the AI built into macOS, violet for a model you downloaded, grey for the tools you drive yourself.
Screenshots and screen captures are flagged automatically.

groups.name: Changed
items: A true 1:1 view — 100 % renders real pixels from the full-resolution file, and panning no longer re-renders what you just looked at.
Develop sliders below the heavy stages no longer re-run everything above them, so Highlights, Shadows and the tone controls respond faster.
Export's enlargement is a plain three-way choice instead of a hidden double negative.
The Noise Reduction slider says it is Apple's, and disables itself on the decode paths where it does nothing.

groups.name: Fixed
items: The mask overlay follows your crop instead of switching itself off.

groups.name: New
items: AI masking in Develop, all on-device — Sky, Object (click to extend, ⌥-click to cut out), People (whole person, or per part: face skin, eyebrows, eyes, lips, teeth, hair, neck, clothing) and Depth (Near/Far sliders), plus Subject and Background built into macOS.
Masks combine — add, subtract or intersect any mask with another, each part still editable.
Feather on AI masks, with an optional outward falloff.
AuraFace face-recognition model, downloadable in Settings ▸ AI. Re-indexing keeps your names.

groups.name: Changed
items: The Masking tab was redesigned — a tile per mask type, a mask list with plain-language summaries, and a drill-in editor showing what each mask is built from.
No models ship with the app — download only what you want in Settings ▸ AI. Each is verified, individually deletable, and shows its licence and credits.
Quick adjust presets moved into the mask editor and merge into a mask instead of replacing it.
The folder you are browsing is highlighted in the sidebar and scrolled into view.
The person menu's "Manage…" sheet highlights the face under your pointer.

groups.name: Fixed
items: "Remove GPS" removes everything — altitude, timestamp, speed and heading are scrubbed too.
A failed export can no longer destroy the file it was overwriting.
Develop edits, versions and Pixels overlays work in multi-folder views, and save into each photo's own folder sidecar.
A failed write of edits or cull state is reported instead of losing the work silently.
Synchronize on an unreachable folder no longer wipes its catalog entries and AI keywords.
Edits made on the hidden twin of a RAW+JPEG pair are no longer dropped.
Switching folders during a metadata write no longer disables all further saving until relaunch.
⌘Z undo of a move to Trash works after you switch folders.
Thumbnail cache files are written atomically; renamed files keep their previews; edited thumbnails re-render when the file changes.
RAW decoding fails gracefully instead of crashing when memory is critically low.
Fixed two freezes — the Vault backup's zip step and JPEG/JXL export encoding.
Update DNG Preview honours "Back up files before writing".
Pixels overlays are included in the off-folder sidecar backups.

groups.name: Changed
items: HDR bracket merge: select an exposure bracket and merge it into a single DNG — automatic alignment, deghosting, and a floating-point linear DNG you can develop like any other RAW.

New comparison modes for culling: Compare (C) puts candidates side by side, Survey (N) lays out the whole selection — both with 1:1 inspection and rating/flagging without leaving the mode. Right-click a burst stack to Survey it in one go.
Blend modes / double exposure in Develop: stack a second image over your photo with opacity and classic blend modes.

New Punch slider in Develop → Presence: the life Lightroom's Dehaze gives flat images — broad local contrast plus a touch of saturation — without the haze-removal side effects. Pull it negative to soften and lay down a gentle fog veil. Independent from Dehaze, Clarity, and Contrast.

The Develop before/after loupe is bigger and now actually magnifies — it shows the "before" enlarged instead of the same size. Zoom the glass with the scroll wheel, the = / - keys, or the on-screen ± buttons (all rebindable in Settings → Shortcuts → "Develop loupe"). Its controls moved to a compact icon column so they no longer overlap the photo.
The catalog now backs itself up automatically when you quit, with a new Backups tab in Settings.
Grid quality-of-life: right-click menu for flags, color labels, and ratings; press the same number again to clear a star rating; bigger maximum thumbnail size; smoother Loupe hover.
Pixels tab: drag layers to reorder them (the list now matches the visual stacking), date stamps and other overlays are draggable again, and the layers list is roomier.
Heal tool: resize the heal circle with the keyboard or scroll wheel.
Tidier menus and controls: one unified View menu, easier-to-click zoom buttons, Makeup sub-sliders that move as a group, and ⌘F now lands the cursor in the search field.

groups.name: Changed
items: Export redesigned: a cleaner dialog with resize, metadata options, presets, and a real File Naming module (custom names + auto sequence) with clearer handling of name collisions.
Export now remembers your last-used settings each time you open it.
New dehaze engine in a dedicated Dehaze block, plus local Dehaze inside masks.
Grid, filmstrip, and lightbox thumbnails now reflect your Develop edits instead of showing the untouched original.
Filmstrip: hover and use the scroll wheel to pan through it.
Faster, smoother Develop, including a preview-quality setting (Full / Half / Quarter) and quicker Fujifilm RAF handling.
Makeup controls tidied — now grouped under Highlights and Shadows.
Mask overlays now hide automatically when you leave the Masking tab.

groups.name: Changed
items: Renamed the app to Chili RAW, with a new icon and identity.
Highlight recovery rebuilt: recover real detail in blown skies and bright edges instead of graying them out.
New Shadows engine for smoother, halo-free shadow lifts.
Added Texture and Makeup controls for fine detail and skin.
New straighten tools: draw a line to level a photo, plus auto-straighten.
Faster, cleaner map: native pins, clustering for big folders, and no lag opening Geo Tag.
Lightbox culling view with dedicated cull shortcuts.
Metadata now saves automatically — no more ⌘S.
Confirmation prompt before deleting, so nothing goes by accident.
Missing files stay in the catalog as "Media Offline" placeholders instead of vanishing.
Many smaller fixes to masks, filters, badges, and the develop info bar.

groups.name: Changed
items: Much faster grid: smooth scrolling through huge folders, background thumbnail prebuild, and smarter caching.
New RAW engine with Adobe DNG and LibRaw decoding for more accurate color on proprietary RAW files.
Choose your look: Standard, AgX, and Neutral tone-mapping tabs.
Film grain module with a live preview, baked into exports.
Dust removal and color grading modules.
Clarity rebuilt for crisp local contrast without halos.
White balance, sharpening, and whites/highlights brought closer to Lightroom.
Selectable UI themes and accent colors (Dark / Neutral Grey · Amber / Blue).

groups.name: Changed
items: Catalog & smart folders: organize, sync, and search your whole library.
AI keywords and keyword search.
People: face recognition with named people.
Stacks, Collections, and Vaults for grouping and backing up work.
Loupe view with focus peaking and quick brushes.
Rate-and-advance culling flow.
Video support alongside photos.
JPEG XL support.
Develop upgrades to dehaze, tone rendering, and display.

groups.name: Changed
items: Core photo browser: grid, ratings, flags, batch rename, search, sort, and reorder.
Geo Tag: place photos on a map, search locations, and add or remove GPS.
EXIF / IPTC metadata viewing and editing.
Support for major RAW formats (ARW, CR2/CR3, NEF, RW2, ORF, RAF).
Develop page: film LUTs, RAW adjustments, dehaze, crop, transform, and export.
Masking: radial, linear, and brush masks.
Configurable keyboard shortcuts.

groups.name: Changed
items: Initial internal build.
